properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued July 5 at 10:02AM EDT until July 5 at 10:30AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...

* Until 1030 AM EDT.

* At 1002 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 9 nm east of T
Tower, moving north at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1100 AM EDT.

* At 959 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 16 nm south of
C Tower to 31 nm southwest of S Tower, moving northeast at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Indiana...

.Major flooding continues on the Pakota River near Princeton. The
river is cresting near 24.0 feet. This is slightly higher than the
crest observed in April, 2025, and almost a foot less than the flood
of record, which occurred in May, 2011. Major flood impacts are
forecast to continue through this weekend, after which water levels
are expected to fall more significantly.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Patoka River near Princeton.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 23.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 9:45 AM CDT Saturday was 24.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
early Thursday morning and continue falling to 10.3 feet
Tuesday, July 14.
